comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue recognition for combined development and IP licensing arrangements
comparisons.peer_summary: For arrangements combining development services and IP licenses, the Company evaluates if the license is distinct; if not distinct, revenue is recognized over time as a single performance obligation, whereas distinct licenses result in point-in-time revenue recognition.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the revenue recognition policies and timing for specific arrangements involving hardware/software or intellectual property (IP), but they focus on different operational contexts. NVDA (Item 8, Note 10) quantifies the balance sheet impact of deferred revenue, specifically highlighting $233 million in customer advances for support, licenses, and cloud services, reflecting the deferred nature of these obligations. In contrast, AMD describes the qualitative accounting policy for combined development and IP licensing arrangements, explaining how revenue is recognized over time or at a point in time depending on whether the license is distinct. While NVDA provides specific monetary figures for deferred revenue components, AMD provides the methodological framework for recognizing revenue from similar IP-based contracts without providing specific deferred revenue balances in this excerpt.

sentences.text: (2)Deferred revenue primarily includes customer advances and deferrals related to support for hardware and software, license and development arrangements, and cloud services. $233 million and $35 million of the balance in fiscal 2024 and 2023 respectively, related to customer advances.
Revenue is recognized upon the transfer of control, over time or at a point in time, depending on the nature of the arrangements.
If the license is not distinct, it is combined with the development services as a single performance obligation and recognized over time.
